evals.prompt: Use the sprint-planning skill. Plan Sprint 16 for TaskFlow. 1-week sprint starting Monday. Team: 3 devs, one of them (Bob) is part-time 50%. Our last 3 sprints completed 18, 22, 20 points. Set a sprint goal, calculate capacity, pick items from backlog, create the cycle. Candidates from the backlog: PROJ-201 (5 points, has acceptance criteria), PROJ-202 (3, has acceptance criteria), PROJ-203 (8, has acceptance criteria), PROJ-204 (13, no acceptance criteria), PROJ-205 (2, blocked by PROJ-204). Walk each candidate through the readiness checklist, and show the create-cycle call and how the items are added and checked. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Full planning ceremony: velocity avg 20 × 0.85 ≈ 17 → adjusted for Bob's 50% (team has 2.5 FTE not 3, so ~14-15 capacity), sprint goal in the 'users can X so that Y' format, item selection honoring DoR, cycle(action=create) call with owned_by, cycle(action=manage_workitems) with add_ids.
expectations: The answer prefers velocity-based capacity (has 3+ sprints history, given by the user) over days-based, and does not re-derive it from the tracker
The answer calculates average velocity (20) and applies 15% buffer (×0.85)
The answer says to adjust capacity for Bob's part-time status (not ignoring it)
The answer says to write a sprint goal in the 'By end of sprint, [users] can [capability] so that [value]' format
The answer says to validate each selected item against DoR (estimated, ≤8 points, has AC, no unresolved blockers)
The answer says to create the cycle via cycle(action=create) with owned_by and description (the goal)
The answer says to add items via cycle(action=manage_workitems) with add_ids (an array of work item UUIDs), then reads them back with cycle(action=list_workitems)

evals.prompt: Use the sprint-planning skill. Calculate next sprint capacity for our team of 5 devs, 2-week sprint. Our last 4 sprints completed 32, 28, 35, 30 points. Alice is on PTO for 3 days. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Uses velocity-based capacity (avg 31.25 × 0.85 ≈ 26.5), then adjusts for PTO (3/50 person-days lost), resulting in ~25 points.
expectations: The answer prefers velocity-based capacity (has history) over days-based
The answer calculates average velocity ~31 points
The answer says to apply 15% buffer (×0.85)
The answer says to subtract proportional PTO (3 person-days out of 50)
The answer says to land on ~24-26 points as the recommended capacity

evals.prompt: Use the sprint-planning skill. I'm planning Sprint 1 for a brand new team. Nobody has ever worked together. Help me set capacity. The team has 5 people, the sprint is 2 weeks and nobody has PTO. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: No velocity history → uses days-based formula with focus factor, then applies first-sprint 60% reduction for learning curve.
expectations: The answer detects no velocity history available
The answer uses days-based formula: team_size × sprint_days × 0.7 × 0.85
The answer says to apply the additional first-sprint reduction to 60% of calculated capacity
The answer warns that Sprint 1 commitment is low-confidence and should be re-calibrated after
